mainEntity.name: How do you write 4 in Roman numerals?

acceptedAnswer.text: IV in standard notation. IIII (additive) is also seen, especially on clock faces.

mainEntity.name: What is the largest Roman numeral?

acceptedAnswer.text: Classical numerals stop at 3,999 (MMMCMXCIX). A bar over a numeral multiplies it by 1,000, which here extends the range to 3,999,999.

mainEntity.name: Is there a zero in Roman numerals?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The Romans had no symbol for zero, though they had the word nulla.
It balances the face visually against VIII, and it has a long tradition. Both IV and IIII are historically valid.
